correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed fractional illumination definition and all boundary strata. The normalized axis-circle measure on the ℓ1² block has mass 4 and illuminates boundary points with weight at least 1; each disk factor has analogous mass 2; tensor pushforward gives a cover of mass 2^n. For the lower bound, the probability witness with one of the two active axes and n−2 active disk coordinates makes every fixed direction hit with probability at most (1/4)(1/2)^{n−2}; Tonelli forces mass at least 2^n. A finite max of complex linear moduli cannot equal |z1|+|z2| on all relative phases, proving non-polydisc status. At zero coordinates the one-sided derivative includes the positive modulus |v_j|; the strict inequalities and cases are handled. No finite experiment substitutes for any step.

originality.rationale: The original preprint and updated full open-access article posit, rather than refute, polydisc-only equality; their sharp polydisc computation and strict zonoid subfamily statements do not imply equality for the two-coordinate complex ℓ1 block. Comparisons include complex crosspolytope/dual-polydisc wording, direct-product and fractional-cover aliases, and public research records on real illumination. The statement is an explicit global counterexample family, not a renamed published corollary. Unindexed equivalent arguments remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Published indexing does not rule out an earlier unindexed or unpublished observation of the ℓ1² product extremizer.
A further independent expert comparison, beyond the full primary article and indexed searches, is not performed.

value.rationale: The exact natural ℓ1²–polydisc product constructs nonpolydisc equality cases in every complex dimension and hence refutes an explicit uniqueness component of a recent foundational conjecture. This changes the possible extremizer classification while leaving the universal upper bound intact. The extremal invariant is fixed by a matched cover and hard-point distribution, not by arbitrary parameters or a textbook restatement.
